answer: Sybil defence works by making each agent identity carry a sunk, non-transferable bond: an agent cannot accept work until it locks real value, and two existing agents must vouch for it by staking their own bond behind it. Cloning a million agents therefore costs a million full bonds, not a million free keypairs, and each voucher backs only a few newcomers. A fake island of identities costs more than its griefing yield, while honest agents keep their grove of reputation unrisked. A lone violet outlier pays the same bond as a swarm, so scale buys an attacker nothing.
